question: Does the NAST 2018 Manila Bay stock-assessment abstract expose a separate site-resolved fish source, and can its totals be added to the 2017 NFRDI experimental-trawl survey?

source.title: Stock assessment of commercially important fish fauna in Manila Bay, Philippines (2012–2015)
source.citation: Bigalbal, N. R. B., Lopez, G. D. V., Torres, F. S. B., & Santos, M. D. (2018). Stock assessment of commercially important fish fauna in Manila Bay, Philippines (2012–2015). Transactions of the National Academy of Science and Technology (Philippines), 40(1), 67.

method.summary: Reviewed the official NAST Transactions proceedings PDF at printed page 67 and its contents entry, then cross-checked the official NAST poster-abstract listing. Compared the abstract's author list, dates, and landing-data methods with the 2017 NFRDI Manila Bay experimental-trawl paper.
accessNotes: The NAST abstract reports fish-landing information collected from January 2012 to December 2015 at 16 landing sites surrounding Manila Bay.
It lists catch per fishing operation, species composition, gear and effort, selected fish size measurements, and number of boats landing per sample day; it reports 27 gear types.
It gives an aggregate 218 fish-and-invertebrate species and names Sardinella gibbosa, Sardinella fimbriata, Rastrelliger brachysoma, Portunus pelagicus, and Sarotherodon melanotheron in its abstract.
The abstract does not provide the 16 landing-site names, species-by-site rows, a sampling-date series, trip-to-capture-locality records, or the underlying landing dataset.
method.reuseFinding: The official abstract is accessible, but no item-specific license or permission to republish its abstract, figures, tables, or underlying landing data was verified. Keep only an attributed synopsis.

sourceFindings.scope: The abstract describes a Manila Bay fishery assessment using landing information from 16 sites around the bay for January 2012–December 2015. It reports 27 gear types and 218 fish-and-invertebrate taxa.
sourceFindings.limits: The publication exposes only an aggregate abstract. It does not state which taxon came from which landing site, when a given taxon was landed, or where a fishing operation captured it.
sourceFindings.attribution: Retain as historical fishery context and a lead to a landing-data source; do not convert its aggregate total into regional occurrence rows.

sourceFindings.scope: The abstract names four taxa among its dominant small-pelagic catch description and separately says Sarotherodon melanotheron was observed in landed catch.
sourceFindings.limits: These are source-reported historical names at aggregate Manila Bay fishery scope. No species-by-site or record-level capture-origin evidence is supplied; taxonomic names have not been independently crosswalked here.
sourceFindings.attribution: Do not treat the reported species names as municipality, estero, river, bay-sector, current-presence, or catchability assertions.

trawlRelationship.overlappingStudyInterval: The NAST abstract's January 2012–December 2015 landing-data interval overlaps the trawl paper's March 2014–October 2015 experimental survey interval.
trawlRelationship.observationFrameComparison: The NAST abstract summarizes fish landings from 16 sites and 27 gears; the 2017 paper reports an experimental otter-trawl survey from 16 predetermined bay stations with 156 tows. Different named sampling frames and methods are described.
trawlRelationship.relationshipDecision: The works may belong to a common NFRDI Manila Bay assessment program and some catch data may overlap, but neither source explicitly establishes that lineage or provides an observation-level crosswalk. Keep separate source records while treating totals and potential catches as non-additive until reconciled.

interpretation: This is a historical, bay-wide fishery-landing summary, not an exact capture-locality dataset. The 16 landing sites cannot be mapped to Cavite, Metro Manila, or other bay sectors from the abstract.
The source is distinct from the experimental-trawl paper in the described observation frame, but shared authors and overlapping years leave possible program/data overlap unresolved.
Do not add the 218 landing-assessment total to the 146 trawl-survey total; they differ in sampling frame, time coverage, and possible overlap.
The aggregate abstract does not supply a complete species list or dated site-level observations. No species assertion, occurrence row, geometry, or public projection is added.
No current abundance, stock status, legal fishing advice, catchability, or safety inference is made.

decision.reason: The NAST abstract confirms a historical landing-data study but omits site-level fish tables and capture origins. Its relationship to the overlapping NFRDI trawl survey is unresolved, so the source is cataloged without additive counts or species rows.

nextActions: Look for an openly accessible full report, landing-site data table, or supplement with the 16 site names and taxon-to-site records.
Compare any retrieved landing data with the 2017 trawl table and the separately published Manila Bay species studies before counting taxa or catches.
Keep Manila Bay shared across L1/L2/L3 and avoid assigning landing ports to capture waters without trip-level provenance.
Continue independent freshwater, brackish, river, lake, wetland, and estero discovery; this source concerns marine capture-fishery landings.

sources.supports: Official NAST Transactions proceedings PDF, including the contents entry and the stock-assessment abstract at printed page 67.
Official NAST listing for the 2018 annual scientific poster abstracts and paper title/author group.
Comparison source for the separate March 2014–October 2015 experimental otter-trawl sampling frame.
